Why take the significant legal risk of posting deepfake porn when there's literally no benefit to the creator? There's also some barriers to joining the community, e.g. the need for a fairly powerful Nvidia graphics card, and as others have mentioned, the technical challenge of getting the software to run at all on Windows or Linux. Even if those hurdles were overcome, making a decent deepfake means spending significant time gathering appropriate video clips and then the hours and days of training, and hoping that the converted video comes out looking OK. I've discarded the converted video in some cases, even after spending days making it.

The community currently consists of the python coders, a handful of active deepfake artists, a few website owners who hope to profit from the free content, and a lot of curious onlookers. The python coders who wrote the software are interested in the AI technology possibilities -- AI coding pays very well these days -- not in making better fantasy celebrity porn. The software really hasn't improved that much or gotten easier to use in the past 6 months, and unless consumers are willing to kick in some cash to the creators see the fantasy porn they want, the dynamics aren't going to changed by advertising.
